title: Returned Payments and Certified Funds — Terms of the Installment Payment Plans
content:
**1. Returned-payment fee.** On every plan of the **Installment Payment Plans** the returned-payment (NSF) fee is 25.00 for each dishonored payment.

**2. Return reasons that carry the fee.** The fee is charged when the bank returns a payment for insufficient funds, because the account was closed, or because the payer stopped payment. These three reasons are the same on every plan.

**3. Lookback.** Returned payments are counted over a rolling 12 months, across every billing plan the customer holds.

**4. Certified funds.** When the count of returned payments in the lookback reaches 2, every open plan of the customer is restricted to certified funds. While restricted, a plan accepts payment only by cashier's check, money order, debit card, credit card or cash.

**5. Returned automatic drafts.** On the Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan and the Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan, after 2 returned automatic drafts in one term the recurring authorization is revoked and the plan becomes the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan. On the other plans this count does not apply (shown as 0).

| Plan | Returned-payment fee | Lookback (months) | Returns for certified funds | Returned drafts that end autopay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Point Two-Pay Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 0 (not applicable) |
| Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 2 |
| Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan | 25.00 | 12 | 2 | 2 |

Certified-funds methods on every plan: cashier's check, money order, debit card, credit card, cash.

**Questions this schedule answers**

*Does a return coded as a bank error carry the 25.00 fee?* No; only the three reasons in clause 2 carry it.

*Hypothetically, a customer has one returned payment on an owner term's plan and, ten months later, a second on a non-owner term's plan. Does the restriction apply?* Yes: both returns fall within the 12-month lookback and the count runs across all of the customer's plans, so the count reaches 2.
